Define a homogeneous list property

Source: R/list.R
property_list_of.Rd

The plural counterpart to property_scalar(), for a list whose every element is an instance of class. A spec type written Stop[] is property_list_of(Stop), where a plain S7::class_list would validate nothing about what the list holds.

Usage

property_list_of(
  class,
  default = quote(list()),
  min_length = 0,
  max_length = Inf
)

Arguments

class

S7 class spec. Base type every element must be an instance of.

default

Any. Passed to S7::new_property(). Defaults to an empty list, so the property is always safe to iterate.

min_length, max_length

Number. Inclusive bounds on length(value). max_length may be Inf for an unbounded list.

Value

An S7 property whose value must be a list of class.

Details

Atomic vectors need no helper here - S7::class_double and S7::class_character already accept a vector of any length, and the scalar presets (class_string, class_float) are what restrict one to length 1.

min_length and max_length express a fixed-arity spec type: a tuple of one to three axes is property_list_of(Axis, min_length = 1, max_length = 3).

Examples

library(S7)
Stop := new_class(properties = list(at = class_float))
Ramp := new_class(properties = list(stops = property_list_of(Stop)))
Ramp(list(Stop(0), Stop(1)))
#> <Ramp>
#>  @ stops: List of 2
#>  .. $ : <Stop>
#>  ..  ..@ at: num 0
#>  .. $ : <Stop>
#>  ..  ..@ at: num 1
